theory.intro: A right pyramid has a flat base and triangular faces meeting at the apex. Its surface area is the base plus every triangular face. Each face's height is the **slant height** $l$, so find that first if it is not marked.
facts: Surface area $=$ area of the base $+$ the areas of all the triangular faces.
Each triangular face has area $\tfrac{1}{2}\times\text{base edge}\times\text{slant height}$.
For a **right square pyramid**, $l=\sqrt{h^{2}+\left(\tfrac{s}{2}\right)^{2}}$, where $h$ is the perpendicular height and $s$ is the base edge length.

For a **right rectangular pyramid**, use half the base dimension perpendicular to the face's base edge. For base dimensions $a$ by $b$, the faces on the $a$ edges have slant height $\sqrt{h^{2}+(b/2)^{2}}$, and the faces on the $b$ edges have slant height $\sqrt{h^{2}+(a/2)^{2}}$, where $h$ is the perpendicular height.
steps: Find the slant height of each face.
Find the area of the base and of each triangular face.
Add them for the total surface area.

workedExamples.solution_text:
Area of the base:
$\begin{aligned} A_{\text{base}}&=8\times8\\&=64\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

Area of the four triangular faces:
$\begin{aligned} A_{\text{triangles}}&=4\times\left(\frac12\times8\times7\right)\\&=112\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

Total surface area:
$\begin{aligned} SA&=64+112\\&=176\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

Area of the base:
$\begin{aligned} A_{\text{base}}&=16\times6\\&=96\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

Area of the triangles on the $16\text{ cm}$ edges:
$\begin{aligned} A_{1}&=2\times\left(\frac12\times16\times5\right)\\&=80\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

Area of the triangles on the $6\text{ cm}$ edges:
$\begin{aligned} A_{2}&=2\times\left(\frac12\times6\times\sqrt{80}\right)\\&=6\sqrt{80}\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

Total surface area:
$\begin{aligned} SA&=96+80+6\sqrt{80}\\&\approx230\text{ cm}^{2}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text: A right square pyramid has base edge $12\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $8\text{ cm}$. Find its total surface area.
A right square pyramid has total surface area $600\text{ cm}^{2}$ and base area $100\text{ cm}^{2}$. Find its perpendicular height to $1$ decimal place.
A right rectangular pyramid has base dimensions $10\text{ cm}$ by $8\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $12\text{ cm}$. Find its total surface area to $1$ decimal place.

foundation.solution_text:
Base: $12\times8=96$
Front and back triangles: $2\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times12\times10\right)=120$
Side triangles: $2\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times8\times\sqrt{120}\right)=87.6356\ldots$
$SA=96+120+8\sqrt{120}$
$\approx304\text{ cm}^{2}$

Base: $20\times10=200$
Front and back triangles: $2\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times20\times13\right)=260$
Side triangles: $2\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times10\times\sqrt{244}\right)=156.2049\ldots$
$SA=200+260+10\sqrt{244}$
$\approx616\text{ cm}^{2}$

foundation.question_text: Find the surface area of a right square pyramid with base edge $9\text{ cm}$ and slant height $8\text{ cm}$.
Find the surface area of a right square pyramid with base edge $14\text{ m}$ and slant height $15\text{ m}$.

development.solution_text:
Half the base edge is $2\text{ cm}$.
$l=\sqrt{6^{2}+2^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{40}$
$=6.3246\ldots\text{ cm}$
Base: $4\times4=16$
Triangular faces: $4\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times4\times6.3246\ldots\right)=50.5964\ldots$
$SA=16+50.5964\ldots$
$\approx66.6\text{ cm}^{2}$

Half the base edge is $8\text{ cm}$.
$l=\sqrt{15^{2}+8^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{289}$
$=17\text{ cm}$
Base: $16\times16=256$
Triangular faces: $4\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times16\times17\right)=544$
$SA=256+544$
$=800\text{ cm}^{2}$

development.question_text: A right square pyramid has base edge $100\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $120\text{ m}$. Find its total surface area, including the base.
development.solution_text:
Half the base edge is $50\text{ m}$.
$l=\sqrt{120^{2}+50^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{16900}$
$=130\text{ m}$
Base: $100\times100=10000$
Triangular faces: $4\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times100\times130\right)=26000$
$SA=10000+26000$
$=36000\text{ m}^{2}$

development.question_text:
A right square pyramid has a surface area of $384\text{ cm}^{2}$ and a base area of $144\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Find its perpendicular height.
development.solution_text:
Base edge: $\sqrt{144}=12\text{ cm}$
Area of the four triangles: $384-144=240$
Area of one triangle: $240\div4=60$
Slant height: $60=\tfrac{1}{2}\times12\times l$, so $l=10\text{ cm}$
Half the base edge is $6\text{ cm}$.
$h=\sqrt{10^{2}-6^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{64}$
$=8\text{ cm}$

development.question_text:
A right square pyramid has a surface area of $4704\text{ m}^{2}$ and a base area of $1764\text{ m}^{2}$.
Find its perpendicular height.
development.solution_text:
Base edge: $\sqrt{1764}=42\text{ m}$
Area of the four triangles: $4704-1764=2940$
Area of one triangle: $2940\div4=735$
Slant height: $735=\tfrac{1}{2}\times42\times l$, so $l=35\text{ m}$
Half the base edge is $21\text{ m}$.
$h=\sqrt{35^{2}-21^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{784}$
$=28\text{ m}$

development.question_text: A right square pyramid has base edge $18\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $12\text{ m}$. Find its total surface area, including the base.
development.solution_text:
Half the base edge is $9\text{ m}$.
$l=\sqrt{12^{2}+9^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{225}$
$=15\text{ m}$
Base: $18\times18=324$
Triangular faces: $4\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times18\times15\right)=540$
$SA=324+540$
$=864\text{ m}^{2}$

mastery.question_text:
A right square pyramid has a surface area of $340\text{ cm}^{2}$ and a base edge of $10\text{ cm}$.
Find its perpendicular height, correct to $1$ decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
Area of the base: $10\times10=100$
Area of the four triangles: $340-100=240$
Slant height: $240=4\times\tfrac{1}{2}\times10\times l=20l$, so $l=12\text{ cm}$
Half the base edge is $5\text{ cm}$.
$h=\sqrt{12^{2}-5^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{119}$
$\approx10.9\text{ cm}$

Half the base edge is $3\text{ cm}$.
$l=\sqrt{10^{2}+3^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{109}\text{ cm}$
Base: $6\times6=36$
Triangular faces: $4\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times6\times\sqrt{109}\right)=12\sqrt{109}=125.2837\ldots$
$SA=36+12\sqrt{109}$
$\approx161.3\text{ cm}^{2}$

The faces on the $16\text{ cm}$ edges rise over half of the $12\text{ cm}$ width ($6\text{ cm}$):
$l_{1}=\sqrt{24^{2}+6^{2}}=\sqrt{612}=24.7386\ldots\text{ cm}$
The faces on the $12\text{ cm}$ edges rise over half of the $16\text{ cm}$ length ($8\text{ cm}$):
$l_{2}=\sqrt{24^{2}+8^{2}}=\sqrt{640}=25.2982\ldots\text{ cm}$
Base: $16\times12=192$
Front and back triangles: $2\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times16\times\sqrt{612}\right)=395.8181\ldots$
Side triangles: $2\times\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\times12\times\sqrt{640}\right)=303.5787\ldots$
$SA=192+395.8181\ldots+303.5787\ldots$
$\approx891.4\text{ cm}^{2}$
